item.title: CFTC files amicus brief backing prediction platforms in Nevada appeal, arguing event contracts are swaps that preempt state gambling laws, JD Supra reports
item.description: - **CFTC files amicus brief backing prediction platforms in Nevada appeal, arguing event contracts are swaps that preempt state gambling laws, JD Supra reports** — A Vinson and Elkins analysis published on JD Supra says the CFTC filed an amicus brief in North American Derivatives Exchange v. Nevada in the Ninth Circuit, arguing sports event contracts traded on CFTC-registered markets are swaps under the Commodity Exchange Act and that state gambling laws are preempted. item.description: - **Australia's ASIC says a retail prediction market is unlikely to pass its public interest test for a market licence** — The Australian Securities and Investments Commission said on October 30 that it is not currently convinced prediction markets for retail clients are in the public interest, with Chair Sarah Court noting the contracts share their all-or-nothing structure with binary options, which ASIC has banned for retail clients until October 2031. item.title: The Favorite Vanished: Game of the Year Flipped in Three Weeks
item.description:
The Favorite Vanished: Game of the Year Flipped in Three Weeks

When Polymarket opened its Golden Joystick Awards Ultimate Game of the Year market on October 13, the race looked settled. Saros led the 18-game field at 78 percent, with 007: First Light next at 50 percent, in a multi-outcome book where rival prices can overlap. Three weeks later, neither number survived.

Read on November 2, the market has a new leader and a new shape. Resident Evil Requiem now fronts the field at 52 percent, priced at 52 cents a share, and 007: First Light has fallen to second at 19 percent. Saros, the 78 percent opening favorite, no longer sits in the top two at all. The market has traded $34.1K in total since launch and is scheduled to resolve on or around November 30, when the award is announced.
